The issue: libgdal.so.34 links both libproj.so.25 and libproj.so.22 (because libspatialite/geotiff from base jammy link libproj22). Having two proj versions loaded causes crash. Actually the mixed proj libs cause crash at exit in UnitOfMeasure destructor. This is a known conflict between ubuntugis gdal and base jammy proj.

The real fix: the ubuntugis PPA GDAL 3.8.4 needs proj 9.3, but base jammy libgeotiff/libspatialite etc still link libproj22. This dual loading causes segfault.

Alternative approach: Avoid the PPA. Use GDAL 3.4.1 from base, but then pip gdal 3.6.2 build fails due to version check. Actually the pip gdal build fails because installed gdal-config is 3.4.1 < 3.6.2.

Better approach: Build from the base but use a different version of the GDAL python package that matches libgdal 3.4.1? The pyproject pins gdal = "3.6.2". Poetry install would use that.

Hmm. Actually, the Docker approach used python:3.10 image with apt libgdal-dev (from debian, version ~3.x). That works there because it's Debian's gdal matching its proj. In this Ubuntu 22.04 the base gdal is 3.4.1 which is too old for the pinned python gdal 3.6.2.

Options:
1. Use conda to install gdal 3.6.2 (but need pip poetry).
2. Compile GDAL 3.6.2 from source - long.
3. Install gdal python package that matches system libgdal - but pinned 3.6.2.
4. Fix the dual-proj issue: The segfault occurs because libgdal.so.34 loads both libproj.so.25 and libproj.so.22. This is because some dependency (libspatialite, libgeotiff, libxerces?) links libproj22. Actually base jammy libgeotiff/libspatialite built against proj22. When ubuntugis gdal installed, they upgraded libgeotiff/libspatialite to PPA versions (I saw libgeotiff-dev, libspatialite8, libgeos-dev upgraded). Let me re-check which PPA packages conflict.

Wait, during libgdal-dev install, ubuntugis upgraded libgeos-dev, libspatialite8, libfreexl, gdal-plugins. Let's check what still pulls libproj22. Let me check which system lib requires libproj.so.22 more thoroughly.

Actually the segfault is at exit in proj destructor - a known issue when two versions of libproj loaded. The fix might be to ensure everything links proj25 by upgrading all geospatial deps from PPA. Or simpler: avoid mixing by removing libproj22. But many base libs depend on it.

Alternative simpler robust approach: use conda/mamba to create an env with gdal 3.6.2 and then pip install the rest? Actually the pip `gdal` package 3.6.2 would need to build against conda gdal. Complicated.

Alternative: Instead of PPA, use apt to install a matching python3-gdal? Not for pip.

Hmm, maybe better: the crash is only at interpreter exit (destructor). The functionality works ("ok 3.8.4" printed, then segfault at exit). For tests, everything ran OK — the tests passed (77 tests OK). The segfault is only on exit after cleanup, and exit code becomes 139. That's concerning but functionally the software works.

But we want a clean installation. Let me try to resolve the dual-proj conflict. Let me identify what links libproj22.

Actually maybe I can just remove libproj22 and see what breaks, but apt may refuse. Let me check reverse deps.

Let me check which packages depend on libproj22.

action.command: apt-cache rdepends libproj22 2>/dev/null | head -30; echo "---who links 22---"; for f in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/*.so*; do if readelf -d "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "libproj.so.22"; then echo "$f"; fi; done 2>/dev/null
